info.name: Paisa API
info.description:
Personal Finance + Expense AI backend.

## Getting started

1. Select the **Paisa - Local** environment (or set `baseUrl` yourself).
2. Run **Auth > Signup** (or **Auth > Login** with the seeded demo account).
   The response test script stores `accessToken` and `refreshToken` automatically,
   so every other request is authenticated with no manual copying.
3. Seeded demo credentials (after `npm run seed`): `demo@paisa.app` / `Paisa@2026`.

Collection-level auth is Bearer `{{accessToken}}`; the public auth endpoints override it with no auth.

## Suggested run order

Auth -> Expenses -> Budgets -> SMS -> Subscriptions > Detect -> Analytics -> Insights.
The insight and analytics endpoints need a few weeks of data to say anything interesting,
so run the seeder first for the full experience.

Upsert. `alertThreshold: 0.8` warns at 80%. Transfers, investments and income are excluded from the overall cap.
Each entry carries spent, remaining, percentageUsed, status and a `pace` block with burn rate, projected month-end spend and the safe daily amount for the rest of the month.

Budget warnings ride along on the write that causes them, in `data.budgetAlerts`, so the client can show the warning immediately. Alerts are edge-triggered: you are told once when you cross 80%, not on every later purchase.

item.name: Groups (Split Expenses)
item.description: Splitwise-style shared expenses. Run 'Create group' first — it stores the group id and the member ids that every other request in this folder depends on. Note that splits and settlements reference GROUP MEMBER ids, not user ids, which is what lets registered users and not-yet-signed-up placeholders be handled identically.

request.description: The literal ledger instead of the simplified plan. This is the view that settles an argument about why you owe something.
Records a real payment between two members. Paying less than the full debt simply leaves the remainder outstanding — there is no partial-settlement flag because balances are derived, not stored.
